MODCR 2  ·  Early Clay Series

Germinating Seeds

c. 1972
Medium
Bronze
Dimensions
8 × 5 × 5 in. (20.3 × 12.7 × 12.7 cm)
Inscriptions
Foundry mark on base: [Tallix / 1972]
Title Source
Artist
Collection
The artist's collection
Bronze
Description

Cast bronze forms suggesting the emergence of life from dormancy — a seed at the precise moment of becoming. The surfaces bear the tactile imprint of the artist's hands, preserving the pressure and decision of direct contact between maker and material.

This work marks an early iteration of a morphological vocabulary that would recur and evolve across five decades of practice. The form distills a deep preoccupation with biological process: germination, cellular division, the latent energy within organic matter at the threshold of growth.

Remarks

The foundry mold for this edition was retained by the artist and used for subsequent casts through 1975. The present work is the first cast of the edition.

Date is approximate, based on studio records and the artist's recollection that the work was cast in the year of the Gertrude Kasle Gallery exhibition. An undated preparatory drawing in graphite (MODCR 2a), also in the artist's collection, records an earlier iteration of the form.
